title: Your opinion doesn't f*cking matter (and neither do your dislikes, according to YouTube)
summary: NH attacks YouTube's removal of public dislike counts, arguing it protects big corporations rather than small creators, removes his feedback, and with comment censorship turns channels into echo chambers of fanboys.
claims: YouTube's dislike removal is presented as protecting small creators but really protects big corporations and news outlets from mass dislikes
He wants visible dislikes because they show him whether a video is good or bad so he can improve; YouTube also deletes comments he cannot restore
Creators who can't take criticism don't belong on YouTube; hiding negativity doesn't remove it, it censors it
Without dissent, comment sections become echo chambers of fanboys, and with no challenge there is no knowledge or innovation
